newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Two reported dead after riot in Indonesian town.
newsitem.headline: Two reported dead after riot in Indonesian town.

text.p: Hundreds of troops patrolled this riot-torn Indonesian town on Friday after a mob looted and set buildings and churches ablaze in a rampage apparently sparked by police brutality.

A military official and local journalists said at least two people -- one a middle-aged ethnic Chinese woman carried from a burnt out shop -- had died in the rioting on Thursday in Tasikmalaya, about 200 km southeast of Jakarta.
"The situation seems pretty much under control, though it is still tense," an eyewitness said.

A policeman said the riot was apparently sparked by a report that police had beaten teachers from an Islamic school. Local news reports said one of the teachers had disciplined the son of a policeman, who summoned them for questioning.
Police and residents estimated about 5,000 people, many of them youths in their teens or early 20s, had run amok in the town, a road and rail transit centre of about 500,000 people.
Troops with rifles and rattan shields patrolled the streets past burned out or damaged buildings and set up road blocks every couple of hundred metres to prevent people moving around.
Car showrooms, banks and stores owned by ethnic Chinese as well as Christian churches were the main targets. A number of looters had apparently come from outside the town.
Military authorities said 126 people had been detained for questioning at military headquarters.
"Most of them are from outside the city and were taken while in stolen vehicles," a soldier said. Many of the vehicles were piled with stolen goods, including televisions and refrigerators.
Local residents put up signs on their premises and vehicles saying "Owned by Moslem" to save their property.

Rioters had scrawled obscenities on walls against the ethnic Chinese -- seen as dominating the economic life of the town. The rioters had also written signs saying "No to Jesus," "No to the Jews", and "Police are super-corrupt".
The Roman Catholic Sacred Heart of Jesus church, which only opened in August, was among the churches gutted. It was not immediately known how many churches were damaged or destroyed.
Three heavily-veiled Moslem women stood looking at the burnt Catholic building on Friday.
"Moslem people do not like the Chinese or people of other religions here as we want Tasikmalaya to be a Moslem town," one of the women said, refusing to give her name.
Abdurrahman Wahid, leader of the Nahdlatul Ulama, Indonesia's largest Moslem organisation with some 30 million members, condemned the violence and called for calm.
In the last major riot in mainly Moslem Indonesia, 25 churches and a temple were burnt down and five people died in October after a mob rampaged in the Situbondo area of East Java.
This riot was sparked by a court case in which a Moslem heretic subsequently received a jail term for blasphemy.

Political and religious analysts say Christian churches become targets for mob violence primarily for economic and social reasons, with Christians -- often ethnic Chinese -- usually the more affluent members of the community.

On Wednesday, Christmas Day, Indonesia's armed forces chief General Feisal Tanjung said conflicts triggered by religious differences were more dangerous than those caused by ethnic and racial differences, the official Antara news agency reported.
